question: In the seconds when a person beside idling petrol scooters can smell the exhaust, which partial-combustion toxics (carbonyls, PAHs, 1,3-butadiene, phenol, HCN, sulphur compounds) are at the nose, and how much of each relative to the simulation's THC or CO tracer?

howToUse.thcBasis: shareOfTHC_pct is a MASS share of exhaust THC, the same convention as the simulation's benzeneFracTHC (THC mass counted as CH1.85, 13.85 g per mol C). Level at the nose = simulated THC (ppmC) x the per-ppmC factor given. 1 ppmC of THC = 0.5665 mg/m3 at 25 C.
howToUse.coBasis: Where a ratio to CO is given (idle data, Nepal), level = simulated CO increment (ppm) x ppbPerPpmCO. Use THC basis first; the CO basis is a cross-check from the only real idle measurement.
howToUse.denominatorCaution: The denominators differ by source: FID THC (Daemme 2016), sum of speciated VOC (Tsai 2003, 2018), NMVOC (EEA), sum of measured hydrocarbons incl. CH4 (Stockwell 2016, which misses heavier species so its shares run high). These differ by up to about 1.5x; the ranges below absorb that.
howToUse.simulationCautions: Carry the simulation's own cautions: one simulated red per case, grid-limited 1-s values, held-wind condition, low to moderate confidence. These ratios add their own (low) confidence on top.

headline: METHOD.md said no idle aldehyde data exist for scooters. That is no longer exactly true. One real idle (start-up plus idling) measurement exists: NAMaSTE, Kathmandu 2015 (Stockwell et al. 2016, supplement Table S4). It covers five carburetted Indian-built four-stroke motorcycles and one 110 cc four-stroke scooter, all without catalysts. Formaldehyde was detected only from the scooter, at 0.54-0.55 g/kg fuel (0.15-0.22 % of its CO mass); it was below detection limit for all five motorcycles. Acetaldehyde, 0.82 g/kg (1.3 % of measured hydrocarbons), was measured for one motorcycle only. Taiwan's own idle-stage carbonyl samples (Tsai et al. 2003, JAWMA, Phase III bikes) exist, but the full text was blocked (tandfonline 403), so their idle values were not read.

Taiwanese driving-cycle data (ECE cycle, which includes idle) put the carbonyls at only 0.9-1.1 % of VOC mass for four-strokes in 2003 (abstract) and 1.8-3.0 % of VOC in 2018 (abstract). Formaldehyde, acetaldehyde and acetone were each about 0.1-0.3 % of VOC.

The EMEP/EEA guidebook (full text) applies petrol-car shares to four-stroke motorcycles, because it has no motorcycle data: formaldehyde 1.7-2.1 %, acetaldehyde 0.6-0.75 %, acrolein 0.16-0.19 %, 1,3-butadiene 0.9-1.4 % of NMVOC. It also uses petrol-car PAH factors for motorcycles.

Used ranges, as a mass share of THC (low / central / high): formaldehyde 0.1 / 1.0 / 2.1 %; acetaldehyde 0.13 / 0.7 / 1.3 %; acrolein 0.05 / 0.17 / 0.4 % (car data only); total carbonyls 0.9 / 2.5 / 4.6 %; 1,3-butadiene 0.12 / 1.0 / 3.2 %; naphthalene 0.3 / 0.9 / 2 % (car data only); benzo[a]pyrene 1e-5 / 5e-5 / 2e-4 % (that is 1e-7 to 2e-6 by mass; car-derived factors only). Per 1 ppmC of THC at the nose, the centrals give about 4.6 ppb formaldehyde, 2.2 ppb acetaldehyde, 0.4 ppb acrolein, 2.6 ppb 1,3-butadiene, 1 ppb naphthalene and 0.0003 ug/m3 (0.3 ng/m3) benzo[a]pyrene.

Idle cross-checks against CO, from Nepal (non-catalyst bikes): 1,3-butadiene 0.11-0.59 % of CO mass (median 0.19 %, 11 tests); hydrogen cyanide 0.06-0.17 % of CO; phenol 0.15-0.81 % of CO. Sulphur compounds (OCS, DMS) were only about 0.001 % of CO, and SO2 was below detection limit. Hydrogen sulphide was not measured in anything opened.

There is no idle PAH emission factor for any scooter or motorcycle in anything read. One Taiwanese four-stroke study (abstract) found that the PAHs at idle were lighter ones (phenanthrene, anthracene, pyrene), probably from unburned fuel, and that benzo[a]pyrene appeared mainly at 30 km/h. That suggests idle benzo[a]pyrene is at or below the cycle-based range, but no number supports it.

chemicals.name: formaldehyde
chemicals.perPpmC: 0.46 / 4.6 / 9.7 ppb per ppmC THC (0.57 / 5.7 / 11.9 ug/m3 per ppmC)
chemicals.coBasis: 0.15-0.22 % of CO mass, from the one idle scooter (Nepal, no catalyst) = 1.4-2.05 ppb per ppm CO. Below detection limit for 5 idle motorcycles, so the motorcycle value is lower by an unknown amount.
chemicals.measuredOn: Low: Taiwan, 25 new and in-use Phase III motorcycles, ECE cycle (includes idle), MTBE petrol, 2003. 0.4-0.7 mg/km against 4-stroke VOC of 344-433 mg/km = 0.12-0.16 %; on a pooled 2-/4-stroke VOC basis 0.07-0.12 % (abstract only). Mid: Brazil, one 150 cc Euro III TWC fuel-injected motorcycle on E22 (22 % ethanol), EU urban cycle. HPLC 0.93 mg/km against THC 182 mg/km = 0.51 %. High: EEA guidebook petrol-car share that it applies to 4-stroke motorcycles, 1.70 % (Euro 1-4) to 2.08 % (conventional) of NMVOC. Idle: Nepal Honda Aviator 4-stroke scooter, start-up plus idle, no catalyst, 0.548 g/kg. Its THC was not measured by canister; scaling its FTIR C1-C4 hydrocarbons (14.7 g/kg) by the canister-measured motorcycle's C1-C4 share (52 %) gives about 28 g/kg THC, so formaldehyde is about 2 % of THC (a derived figure, one vehicle).
chemicals.confidence: low: four independent values span 20x; the only idle value is one scooter without a catalyst; Taiwanese idle-stage values exist but were not readable

chemicals.name: acetaldehyde
chemicals.perPpmC: 0.41 / 2.2 / 4.1 ppb per ppmC THC (0.74 / 4.0 / 7.4 ug/m3 per ppmC)
chemicals.coBasis: 0.11 % of CO mass (one idle motorcycle, Nepal) = 0.7 ppb per ppm CO
chemicals.measuredOn: Low: Taiwan Phase III motorcycles, ECE cycle, 0.6-1.2 mg/km against VOC 344-433 (4-stroke) mg/km = 0.17-0.28 %; pooled-VOC basis 0.13 % (abstract only). Mid: EEA petrol-car share applied to motorcycles, 0.59-0.75 % of NMVOC. High: Nepal Bajaj Pulsar 4-stroke, start-up plus idle, no catalyst, canister 0.817 g/kg against 64.1 g/kg summed hydrocarbons = 1.27 % (an upper-leaning share, because the summed hydrocarbons miss heavier species). Brazil E22 1.6 % of THC NOT used for the range: ethanol in the fuel raises acetaldehyde, and Taiwanese petrol is not an ethanol blend.

chemicals.name: acrolein
chemicals.perPpmC: 0.12 / 0.42 / 0.99 ppb per ppmC THC (0.28 / 0.96 / 2.3 ug/m3 per ppmC)
chemicals.measuredOn: PETROL-CAR DATA ONLY. EEA guidebook Table 3-86b: 0.16 % (conventional) and 0.19 % (Euro 1-4) of NMVOC, which the guidebook applies to 4-stroke motorcycles. Table 3-86d: 0.18 % (Euro 5) and 0.08 % (Euro 6). The range is widened by about 2-3x either way because no scooter or motorcycle measurement was opened. A Taiwanese motorcycle study names acrolein among the major carbonyls, but that was seen only in a search snippet, not read. Acrolein is not in NAMaSTE's FTIR or canister lists.

chemicals.name: other aldehydes and ketones (benzaldehyde, tolualdehydes, propionaldehyde, crotonaldehyde, butanal, acetone, butanone)
chemicals.shareBasis: mass share of THC (%) per species
chemicals.central: acetone 0.5; benzaldehyde 0.4; tolualdehydes (sum) 0.5; propionaldehyde 0.08; butanal 0.07; crotonaldehyde 0.03
chemicals.measuredOn: Acetone: Taiwan ECE cycle 0.5-0.7 mg/km = 0.07-0.16 % of VOC (abstract); Nepal idle motorcycle 1.11 g/kg = 1.74 % of summed hydrocarbons; EEA car 0.21-0.61 %. Butanal 0.062 g/kg (0.10 %) and butanone 0.0023 g/kg (0.004 %) for the Nepal idle motorcycle. Benzaldehyde (0.22-0.60 %), o/m/p-tolualdehyde (sum 0.26-0.76 %), propionaldehyde (0.05-0.11 %) and crotonaldehyde (0.02-0.04 %) come from EEA petrol-car data only.

chemicals.name: total carbonyls (aldehydes + ketones)
chemicals.measuredOn: Taiwan 4-stroke, ECE cycle, 2003: 3.1 (new) and 4.6 (in-use) mg/km against VOC 344 and 433 mg/km = 0.90 and 1.06 % (abstract). Taiwan Phase III-V four-strokes, ECE cycle, 2018: carbonyls 1.8-3.0 % of 67-VOC mass (abstract). Nepal idle motorcycle: acetaldehyde + acetone + butanal + butanone + hydroxyacetone = 2.64 g/kg = 4.1 % of summed hydrocarbons, with formaldehyde below detection limit. EEA petrol car: sum of aldehydes and ketones 4.6 % (conventional), 4.0 % (Euro 1-4). This replaces METHOD.md's assumed 0.5-3 % aldehydes of VOC: the measured carbonyl range is somewhat higher at the top.
chemicals.confidence: low to moderate (several independent sources agree within about 5x)

chemicals.name: 1,3-butadiene
chemicals.perPpmC: 0.31 / 2.6 / 8.2 ppb per ppmC THC (0.68 / 5.7 / 18 ug/m3 per ppmC)
chemicals.coBasis: Idle, Nepal, 11 tests on 6 four-stroke two-wheelers (no catalyst): 0.109-0.593 % of CO mass, median 0.190 % = 0.56 / 0.98 / 3.07 ppb per ppm CO (low / median / high)
chemicals.measuredOn: Idle: NAMaSTE fleet average 1.30 (pre-service) and 1.19 (post-service) g/kg fuel (FTIR, Table 1). One canister-sampled motorcycle: 2.04 g/kg = 3.18 % of summed hydrocarbons (high end). EEA petrol car: 1.42 % (conventional), 0.91 % (Euro 1-4), 0.12 % (Euro 5), 0.80 % (Euro 6) of NMVOC. The Euro 5 figure sets the low end. Researcher 1 may also cover this species; this entry is the partial-combustion view.
chemicals.confidence: low to moderate (a real idle measurement exists, but on non-catalyst Indian bikes)

chemicals.name: naphthalene (gas-phase, the largest PAH)
chemicals.perPpmC: 0.32 / 0.97 / 2.2 ppb per ppmC THC (1.7 / 5.1 / 11 ug/m3 per ppmC)
chemicals.measuredOn: PETROL-CAR DATA ONLY: EEA Table 3-86d (from Marques et al. 2022), 0.95 % (Euro 5) and 0.84 % (Euro 6) of NMVOC. Widened about 2-3x because no motorcycle naphthalene share was read. A Taiwanese dynamometer study (Yang et al. 2005, Atmos Environ) reports that naphthalene dominates motorcycle PAHs, but only search-engine snippets were seen, so it is not used.

chemicals.name: benzo[a]pyrene (particle-bound)
chemicals.measuredOn: EEA Table 3-26: 4-stroke motorcycles <250 cc, B(a)P 4.80e-7 g/km (conventional) and 3.20e-7 g/km (Euro 1 and later). Table 3-25 NMVOC for the same class: 1.375 (conventional), 1.041 (Euro 1), 0.490 (Euro 2), 0.179 (Euro 3), 0.177 (Euro 4), 0.522 (Euro 5) g/km. The ratio is 3.1e-7 to 1.8e-6 by mass. The guidebook states that these PAH factors are petrol-car factors applied to motorcycles, and the ratio rises at Euro 3-4 only because BaP is held fixed while NMVOC falls. Measured on a Taiwanese 4-stroke motorcycle (cycle, particle phase, abstract only): BaP-equivalent 70.8 +- 38.4 ng/km, with no matching THC in the abstract, so no ratio. Idle: lighter PAHs dominated; BaP formed mainly at 30 km/h (abstract, qualitative).
chemicals.confidence: very low: car-derived factors and no idle number. No seconds-long reference value exists for BaP; its guidelines are annual means.

chemicals.name: phenol
chemicals.coBasis: Idle, Nepal (FTIR): 0.15-0.81 % of CO mass over 11 tests
chemicals.measuredOn: Idle Nepal non-catalyst 4-strokes: fleet averages 4.84 (pre) and 3.02 (post) g/kg; for the canister-sampled bike, 3.44 g/kg = 5.4 % of summed hydrocarbons. EEA Euro 5/6 petrol car (Marques 2022): 0.01-0.05 % of NMVOC. The two disagree by about 100x. This is not resolved, so the central value is only an order of magnitude.

chemicals.name: hydrogen cyanide
chemicals.measuredOn: Idle Nepal, FTIR, 10 of 11 tests above detection limit: 0.20-1.40 g/kg, 0.061-0.166 % of CO mass. Fleet average 0.841 (pre) and 0.678 (post) g/kg. Non-catalyst bikes; a working catalyst should remove much of it, but no catalysed measurement was found.

chemicals.name: sulphur compounds (OCS, DMS, SO2)
chemicals.measuredOn: Idle Nepal: one canister-sampled bike, OCS 0.0102 g/kg and DMS 0.0049 g/kg; SO2 below detection limit in all FTIR tests. This is negligible beside CO. Hydrogen sulphide (the after-catalyst 'rotten egg' smell) was not measured in any source opened.

notEstimated.name: hydrogen sulphide (H2S)
notEstimated.why: No measurement in scooter, motorcycle or car exhaust was opened. Taiwanese petrol is low-sulphur (not checked here). No guess is made.

notEstimated.name: sum of the 16 US-EPA PAHs
notEstimated.why: Only car-derived per-km factors for individual PAHs (EEA) and a Taiwanese motorcycle study whose abstract was seen only as a search snippet; no matching THC, so no defensible ratio. Naphthalene and BaP are given separately.

notEstimated.name: nitro-PAHs, oxy-PAHs, dioxins
notEstimated.why: Motorcycle studies exist (e.g. Pham 2013; AAQR dioxin studies), but none was readable (sciencedirect and aaqr blocked) and they are particle-phase traces irrelevant to the smell.

notEstimated.name: idle-specific Taiwanese carbonyl values
notEstimated.why: Tsai et al. 2003 (JAWMA) sampled the idle stage separately, but the full text is on tandfonline.com, which returned 403. Tsai, Chiang & Hsu 2003 (Atmos Environ 37:2485, VOC by driving mode) is on sciencedirect.com, also 403, and no abstract was available. Not worked around.

blockedOrMissing: tandfonline.com returned HTTP 403: Tsai et al. 2003 JAWMA full text (it holds idle-stage carbonyl data for Taiwanese motorcycles) and Ho et al. 2012 JAWMA (Hong Kong carbonyls). Not worked around.
aaqr.org returned HTTP 403: Tsai 2017 and 2018, Yao 2017, Tsai 2019, Yang 2005 full texts; abstracts were used where available.

sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403: Yang et al. 2005 Atmos Environ 39:17 (motorcycle PAH factors, naphthalene); Tsai, Chiang & Hsu 2003 Atmos Environ 37:2485 (VOC by driving mode including idle); the 2022 high-performance-motorcycle study; the 2019 E0-E50 two-wheeler study. No abstracts were obtainable for the Elsevier papers (elided in the open metadata).

mdpi.com returned HTTP 403: Tsai, Chen & Chiang 2023 (Taiwan mobile-source toxics inventory). Only the abstract was read via OpenAlex; it gives no numbers (the inventory is modelled with MOVES and speciation, not measured).
No measurement of H2S, acrolein or naphthalene from scooters or motorcycles was readable.
notesForIntegrator: Hazard labels (IARC groups) were not researched here; whoever adds them should cite IARC directly and present them as hazard labels only.

Reference values: if a comparison is made, use only ones with matching averaging times. For example, formaldehyde has WHO 100 ug/m3 (30 min) and acrolein has OEHHA 2.5 ug/m3 (1 h); both are already in METHOD.md. 1,3-butadiene, naphthalene and BaP have only long-term (annual or chronic) values in what the project has used, so a seconds-long level must not be set beside them.

The catalyst matters: in Daemme 2016 the catalyst removed about 95 % of steady-state formaldehyde (7.58 to 0.35 mg/km). The Nepal idle data are from bikes without catalysts, so the Nepal ratios to CO are not automatically valid for catalysed Taiwanese scooters. A catalyst lowers CO and HC as well, so the ratio may shift either way.

Sanity check against the existing estimate: the canister-sampled Nepal idle bike gives benzene 3.3 % of summed hydrocarbons, against the estimate's benzene share of THC (0.7 to 6 %, central 2.5 %); consistent.
